worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+2b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $2b.$ So, we first draw the vector $2b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041137/assets/1d266a8324d18191f5bc8560be6539d54d1a11916f33ead7432d9f528769fc22.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $2b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=\frac{1}{2}|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=\frac{1}{2}a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =2b+\frac{1}{2}a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+2b=\frac{1}{2}a+2b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =\frac{1}{2}.
$$
